 Scams loom as Medicare open enrollment gets underway 
 Open enrollment runs until Dec. 7 for people 65 and older 
 Open enrollment runs until Dec. 7 for people 65 and older By Austin Johnson Published : Oct. 28, 2026 at 4:50 AM CDT | Updated : 7 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google QUINCY (WGEM) - The Quincy Better Business Bureau is sharing tips to avoid scams during Medicare open enrollment, when people 65 and older can add, switch or drop services or enroll in 2027 Medicare benefits.
 Scammers try to trick people into sharing personal or financial information during this time. According to July data released by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, 70.7 million people are enrolled in Medicare.
 The Quincy BBB said people should be skeptical of those who contact randomly and of callers who promise gifts. The BBB said anyone who thinks they are being scammed should go directly to official websites and avoid suspicious links or newly created websites.
 BBB warns of scams as Medicare open enrollment gets underway. (WGEM) Don O’Brien, the Quincy BBB regional director, said he has seen how enrollment confuses people, especially those who have just reached the age to qualify.
 “If you’re using this for the first time, you don’t know they aren’t supposed to charge you for this help. You think, well, that’s what I gotta pay for someone to help me – I pay for my mechanic, I pay for my doctor, I gotta do co-pays, so maybe there’s a co-pay involved; there’s none of those things,” O’Brien said.
 “So, someone calls you and says, ‘Hey, I can help you with a Medicare plan; just pay me 100 or whatever, and we will figure out what’s best for you.’ Don’t do that because there are people out there that can help you for free,” O’Brien said.
 HealthCare.gov and Medicare.gov have people sometimes called navigators or assisters. Their job is to help determine the right plan.
 The BBB advises people to guard their government-issued numbers. It recommends never revealing a Medicare ID number, Social Security number, health plan information, or banking information to anyone they do not know.
 Open enrollment runs until Dec. 7. Approved changes will take effect in January.
 Medicare Advantage open enrollment is from Jan. 1 to March 31.
 HealthCare.gov open enrollment starts Nov. 1.
